input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator condition was inverted when the code moved into get_help_spec: it now uses "; " when any_prefix_is_slash is false and " / " when it is true, which is the reverse of the original logic.
- rationale: Trigger: any option whose spellings use a slash prefix, such as a boolean flag declared as "--shout/--no-shout", or any option without slash prefixes. Mechanism: the join separator is swapped, so slash-style options render with "; " and ordinary options render with " / ". Impact: the help output's left column is wrong for these options, and the regression is visible in every help page that lists them.
critique: The finding names the same fault as the label: the separator condition on any_prefix_is_slash is inverted, so '; ' is used when it is false and ' / ' when it is true. The rationale garbles the impact, mislabeling --shout/--no-shout as slash-prefixed and stating the swap backwards, but the root cause and mechanism are the same.
